name: University of Melbourne — Melbourne Law School
tech_center: Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Ethics (CAIDE, with Engineering & IT; renewed to 2030)
highlights: Deep AI/tech-law catalogue: Artificial Intelligence and the Law, Legal AI: Design and Development (students build LLM-based legal apps), AI and Justice, International Law and AI (2026), plus undergraduate AI Ethics and the Law
Pioneering Law Apps clinic (est. 2015): JD teams built and released live Neota Logic apps for not-for-profits for a decade
Specialist Certificate and Melbourne Law Masters stream in Digital Law and Technological Innovation
Law Apps Bake Off pitch nights; hackathon with King & Wood Mallesons; CAIDE delivers AI-literacy training across Australia/NZ
caveats: The flagship Law Apps clinic is listed as not offered in 2026; hands-on building has shifted to the generative-AI subject LAWS90286.

name: UNSW Sydney — Faculty of Law & Justice
highlights: Designing Technology Solutions for Access to Justice: project-based course where student teams build legal apps for not-for-profits (Gilbert + Tobin / Neota Logic supported)
2026 handbook AI courses: Artificial Intelligence: Law and Governance; Big Tech, AI and the Law; comparative law-and-tech course with University of Zurich
Strong faculty bench: Lyria Bennett Moses (AI regulation, AI in courts), Michael Legg (AI and the profession)
Kingsford Legal Centre provides clinical legal education
caveats: The Allens Hub — long the flagship legal-tech centre — closed 1 June 2024 with no named successor; older sources describing it as active are out of date.

name: University of Technology Sydney (UTS) — Faculty of Law
tech_center: Hosts AustLII (Australasian Legal Information Institute), a major legal-informatics institution
highlights: Legal Futures and Technology major in the LLB — an Australian first — with an applied tech project capstone and legal-tech internships (LawPath, AustLII, Westpac, Marrickville Legal Centre)
Allens Neota UTS Law Tech Challenge for Social Justice, running since 2016: student teams build AI-driven apps for non-profits with Allens mentoring
Bachelor of IT / Bachelor of Laws dual degree; first Sydney university to offer Practical Legal Training in-house
Disruptive Technologies and the Law elective covers AI in practice, e-discovery, and emerging-tech regulation

name: Swinburne University of Technology — Swinburne Law School
tech_center: Legal Tech Clinic and Legal Design Clinic (Dr Mitchell Adams)
highlights: Legal Tech Clinic builds solutions for real law firm clients (e.g., 2025 warranty-claim triage prototype for CIE Legal)
Only Victorian law school with compulsory professional experience: three 20-day accredited placements in every LLB, with a ~200-organisation placement network
Flagship Legal Technology and Innovation unit covers computational legal thinking, generative AI, and human-centred legal design with hands-on building
LLB / Computer Science double degree (AI options); concurrent PLT via Leo Cussen accelerates admission

name: Flinders University — College of Business, Government and Law
highlights: Australia's first compulsory app-building law topic: every LLB student takes Law in a Digital Age, where law + CS teams build real legal apps and chatbots (Docassemble, Neota Logic) for access-to-justice clients — 60+ apps built
Unusual end-to-end pipeline: apps built in class are deployed and maintained by the Digital Law Lab and used by the Flinders Legal Centre community clinic
LLB (Honours) Legal Practice Entry satisfies academic admission requirements Australia-wide; semester-long industry placements
caveats: No legal-tech degree/certificate, standalone AI-law course, or recurring hackathon.

name: University of Auckland — Auckland Law School
tech_center: Centre for Advancing Law and Technology Responsibly (ALTeR, with Business & Economics)
highlights: ALTeR — a new active centre with a dedicated Chair in Law and Technology (Prof Alexandra Andhov) researching AI governance, Big Tech accountability, and govtech
Named AI electives: Law and Artificial Intelligence; Technology Law and Policy
ALTeR legal tech hackathon (2025): interdisciplinary teams prototyped an AI legal assistant for access to justice
caveats: No legal-tech degree and no permanent build-and-deploy clinic; NZ professional training happens after the LLB through external providers.
